items.title: Grafana 13.3 release: manage variables across dashboards, share findings with Notebooks, a UI refresh, and more
items.summary: Grafana 13.3 is here, bringing more consistency and control to how you work across Grafana. Cross-dashboard variables help you manage shared dashboard controls from one place, while Notebooks let you capture and share findings from across Grafana in a single, editable document. You'll also get a first look at Grafana's biggest visual refresh since Grafana 7, along with new ways to guide and refine dashboards built with Grafana Assistant.Below are just some of the highlights from this release. You can explore all of the updates in the changelog or our What's new in Grafana 13.3 documentation.Define a variable once and use it across dashboardsAvailable in public preview in all editions of GrafanaWhen multiple dashboards use the same variable, such as an environment, region, or cluster selector, managing it separately in each dashboard creates duplicate work and can lead to configuration drift. To address this, we’re rolling out cross-dashboard variables, which let you define a variable once and reuse it across dashboards in your Grafana organization.You can create and manage these variables from Dashboards > Variables, and scope each one as either:Global: available to every dashboard in the organizationFolder: available only to dashboards in the same folderWhen you edit a dashboard, add a variable from the sidebar and select Global or folder variable. Grafana shows only the variables available to that dashboard's scope, and you can add them one at a time or all at once. Viewers can still change the variable's value on the dashboard, while its configuration stays managed centrally, so shared controls stay consistent without editing every dashboard that uses them.To try cross-dashboard variables in self-managed Grafana, enable the grafana.dashboardGlobalVariables feature toggle. To learn more, refer to the cross-dashboard variables documentation.Consolidate and share your findings with NotebooksAvailable in public preview in all editions of GrafanaAn investigation rarely happens in one place. You might start on a dashboard panel, jump into Explore to run a query, and then ask Grafana Assistant what's going on. Until now, the evidence and your reasoning ended up scattered across tabs, screenshots, and chat threads.Notebooks let you capture findings from across Grafana in a single, editable document. Add panels from dashboards or Explore, pull in findings from Grafana Assistant, and write your observations right next to the data. Teammates can then follow your investigation, understand how you reached your conclusions, and collaborate on next steps.You can use a notebook to:Explore a question about your data, keeping queries and notes side by side as your thinking develops.Document an investigation so the next person doesn't have to start from scratch.Prepare a post-incident review with the relevant panels already in place.You can create notebooks manually or with Grafana Assistant, then save and share them for future reference. The new Notebooks page also makes it easy to find and manage your work, with options to search, filter, edit, and export notebooks. Notebooks are gradually rolling out to Grafana Cloud. To try them in self-managed Grafana, enable the dashboard.notebooks feature toggle. To learn more, refer to the Notebooks documentation.A fresh new look for the Grafana UIAvailable in public preview in all editions of GrafanaWhether it’s adding new data sources or supporting new use cases, we’re constantly expanding what Grafana can do. And as AI-powered workflows with Grafana Assistant became a bigger part of how people use Grafana every day, we saw an opportunity to rethink how the platform looks and feels.With Grafana 13.3, we're introducing the first phase of our biggest visual refresh since Grafana 7. Built on an updated set of design principles, the refresh introduces new colors, typography, and UI components to create a more modern, consistent experience across Grafana.Updates include: New default dark and light themes. We've reworked every theme color, with more shades for flexibility, and main action buttons now have a solid, high-contrast style.Softer borders and floating components. Rounder corners offer a more modern feel, and subtle borders on cards, panels, and drawers create a clearer sense of depth. The toolbar and navigation also stand apart more clearly from page content.Updated inputs, drop-downs, buttons, and tags. We've resized our most-used components to be more proportional and consistent. Revised typography. A new type scale mixes font weights and sizes, rather than relying on size alone, so it's easier to see what matters most on a page. Importantly, this is a visual refresh, not a redesign. Your existing workflows and navigation stay the same, and there are no breaking changes for plugins.
